$description: Accepted market overrides for the iOS header band and Android status bar (DEC-15). Karl accepted every suggested override on 2026-11-05: these markets keep the color their app ships instead of following navbar. Read by scripts/build_tokens.py (override tokens) and scripts/build_shell_colors.py (docs). The value always comes from the shipped data, never from this file.

notes.statusbar: Apps team (Ameer M., 2026-11-05 from code; confirmed on device 2026-11-10): on Android 14 and below the status-bar icons are white (main theme never sets windowLightStatusBar), so these dark overrides are needed; on Android 15+ the app shows a white status bar with dark icons in these markets (= navbar, the majority).

statusbar_icons.$description: Android status-bar icon style per Android version (DEC-15, Karl 2026-11-06: build both versions once confirmed on a device). Read by scripts/build_tokens.py (statusbar.android.<m>.icons / icons15) and scripts/build_shell_colors.py (docs, Figma samples). 'light' = white icons (windowLightStatusBar off), 'dark' = dark icons (windowLightStatusBar on). The icon colors themselves are drawn by the system.

android14.confirmed: Ameer M. (Apps team), on device 2026-11-10: the main theme never sets windowLightStatusBar (only splash and onboarding do)

android15.dark_confirmed: Ameer M. (Apps team), on device 2026-11-10: white status bar (= navbar) with dark icons in these markets
android15.others_note: Not confirmed: the Apps team only described the 7 white-top-bar markets. Inferred: every other market keeps navbar with light icons (its navbar passes 3:1 with white; lowest TDCD 3.01:1). Ask Apps team (MISSING-ASSETS 5.6).
